Everything below is open source. Where a tool is published, the paper is on the
[publications](publications.qmd) page.

## EWAS-Galaxy / `ewastools`

A tool suite for population epigenetics integrated into Galaxy: an end-to-end workflow
for Illumina Infinium methylation arrays that a researcher can run without writing code,
from `.idat` import through quality control to differentially methylated position and
region calling. Distributed through the Galaxy ToolShed with Docker images, and published
in *GigaScience* (2020).

[Repository](https://github.com/kkamieniecka/ewas_galaxy) ·
[Paper](https://doi.org/10.1093/gigascience/giaa049)

## `ewas-crossarray-harmonise`

Reproducible cross-array harmonisation and region detection for longitudinal EWAS,
written in R. The implementation side of the doctoral framework for combining Illumina
450K and EPIC data in one analysis.

[Repository](https://github.com/kkamieniecka/ewas-crossarray-harmonise)

## `hurdle-nanomethvar`

A modular, Docker-based Nextflow DSL2 pipeline for Nanopore data, covering methylation
calling and variant analysis in one reproducible workflow.

[Repository](https://github.com/kkamieniecka/hurdle-nanomethvar)

## `pgxBridge`

An R-based pharmacogenomic workflow connecting variant data to interpretable prescribing
recommendations. In development as part of the thesis.

## RNA-Seq data readiness for machine learning

Training and reference material on preparing RNA-Seq data for machine learning
applications — what has to be true of a count matrix before a model is worth fitting.

[Repository](https://github.com/kkamieniecka/rna-seq-data-for-ml)

## `audio-abstracts`

A small utility that reads research abstracts aloud via the ElevenLabs API, with the
scientific jargon handled so that it is actually listenable.

[Repository](https://github.com/kkamieniecka/audio-abstracts)
